_comment: Copy this file to ~/.config/agentic-mouse/config.json and fill in the
Every REPLACE_ME_* value below is a placeholder. The loader recognises them
and treats the corresponding feature as unconfigured rather than trying to
use them, so an unedited copy of this file is harmless.
Nothing in this example is a real bridge address, light id, device id or
application key, and none of those may ever be committed to this repository.
Run `agentic-mouse-doctor config` to see the resolved configuration, fully

_comment_bridgeHost: The bridge's IP address or its <bridge-id>.local name, on your LAN.
Find it in the Hue app under Settings -> My Hue System -> your bridge.
_comment_applicationKeySource: Where the hue-application-key comes from. 'keychain' is strongly
preferred; see docs/SETUP.md for the one-line `security` command that
_comment_lights: The four chosen Hue lights, split into the two clusters that drive the
`resourceIdentifier` is a Hue v2 light resource UUID. List yours with:
`label` is free text, only used in the menu and the doctor output.
`weight` biases a lamp inside its cluster; leave it at 1.0 normally.
_comment_brightness: brightnessFloor keeps a lamp at 1% from making the mouse look broken.
brightnessGamma < 1 lifts the low end, because Hue reports brightness
roughly perceptually while LEDs respond roughly linearly.
_comment_offPolicy: What a zone does when every lamp in its cluster is off:
blackout     - the zone goes dark, mirroring the room (default)
releaseLayer - the zone becomes translucent and iCUE takes it back
dimLastColor - a faint hint of the last colour

_comment_device: Which mouse may be painted. Matching is case-insensitive and every
substring must appear in the model name. `deviceTag` optionally pins one
exact unit by its redacted hash (printed by `agentic-mouse-doctor icue`), so a
specific mouse can be chosen without ever writing its real id to disk.
requiresUniqueMatch refuses to guess when several mice match.
_comment_layerPriority: iCUE itself renders at 127 and other shared SDK clients default to 128,
so 130 puts the companion on top. This is still a SHARED layer - the
project never requests exclusive lighting control.
_comment_sdkSearchPaths: Extra places to look for the proprietary iCUE SDK, tried before the
built-in list. The SDK is never bundled with this project.

multiTap._comment_multiTapTimeout: Seconds after the last tap before the letter commits.
multiTap._comment_holdThreshold: Press duration that counts as a long press (digits, Return, case cycle).
_comment_echoPolicy: commitOnly  - buffered. Nothing reaches the app until the letter commits;
the HUD shows what is pending. This is the safe default.
livePreview - expert opt-in. Types each letter immediately and rewrites it
with real backspaces as you cycle. Still target-anchored,
but it edits a live document.
_comment_focusChangePolicy: cancelPending        - drop the half-typed letter, stay in the mode
cancelPendingAndExit - drop it and leave multi-tap mode entirely
multiTap._comment_autoExitAfterIdle: Seconds of no input before the mode exits itself. 0 disables.

_comment_transport: icueMacroKey - the production route. Raw CorsairKeyEvents from the exact
Scimitar, suppressed while the mode is active via
cgEventTap   - documented fallback only. It cannot tell one physical mouse
input._comment_gridMacroKeys: The audited Scimitar reports CMKI_1 ... CMKI_12.
input._comment_toggleKey: Side button 12 enters and exits the mode. It displaces no applied normal action.
_comment_fallbackBindings: Only used when transport is cgEventTap. Maps each grid key name (k1..k12)
to whatever CGEvent the button produces under your iCUE profile, e.g.
"k2": {"kind": "keyCode", "keyCode": 107, "modifiers": ""} (F14; F13/F17/F18 are reserved by VS Code)

hud._comment: corner: topLeft | topRight | bottomLeft | bottomRight | center
